narrative.headline: Gukesh spends six minutes on a book move
narrative.text: Gukesh played 8.Rb1, a known opening-book move that the engine also rates as its top choice, keeping the evaluation steady at about +0.13 pawns. The move came right after Sindarov's 7...Qb6, a queen move that may have prompted Gukesh to double-check how to meet it. The engine saw at least 5 good moves, including queen moves like Qc2 and Qb3, so Gukesh probably weighed a rook move against those queen options. The engine's main line with Rb1 leads to trades on d7, which may have been part of what Gukesh was assessing. At 6m 10s this was only Gukesh's fourth-longest think, and with 1h 52m left against Sindarov's 1h 54m, the clock was no concern.

likely_reasons.reason: Sindarov's 7...Qb6 put the queen on b6, and Gukesh probably wanted to choose carefully between the rook reply and queen moves like Qc2 or Qb3.
With at least 5 good moves available and a low difficulty rating, there was no single forced answer, so Gukesh may have been comparing several sound options.
The game was still in known theory and Gukesh had plenty of time, so a moderate refresh of preparation cost little.

narrative.headline: Sindarov leaves theory with a quiet Qd8
narrative.text: Javokhir Sindarov spent 2 minutes 41 seconds on 11...Qd8, a queen retreat that was a novelty and took the game out of the opening database. The engine rated it the second-best move, with a tiny edge for the bishop retreat Be8, and the evaluation barely moved from -0.05 to -0.09. With at least 5 good moves available and none of them trading pieces or committing the pawn structure, the decision was low-risk but open-ended, which may explain a moderate think rather than a long one. Sindarov was also probably taking a moment to get oriented after stepping out of known theory, right after Gukesh had spent over four minutes on 11.Bd3. The clock was no worry: Sindarov went from 1h 52m to 1h 49m and still held a lead over Gukesh's 1h 43m.

likely_reasons.reason: Sindarov was the one leaving opening theory with a novelty, so a short check of the new position was likely natural.
There were at least five good, quiet options with no captures or pawn commitments, so the choice between them was probably a matter of taste rather than calculation.
A comfortable clock lead may have let Sindarov spend a few minutes without pressure.

narrative.headline: Sindarov spends time on a quiet bishop retreat
narrative.text: Sindarov played 13...Be8, a bishop retreat the engine ranks as its second choice and classifies as a good move, with the evaluation shifting only slightly from -0.11 to -0.23 for Sindarov. The engine preferred the pawn move a5, and a6 was also close, so there were at least 5 good moves on the table and no single forced answer. One likely reason for the 4m 31s think is that the main alternatives were pawn moves that commit the pawn structure, while Be8 keeps the structure flexible, a choice that may have needed weighing. The game was only two moves out of known theory after Sindarov's own 11...Qd8, so Sindarov was probably still working things out at the board, having already spent 10m 43s on 12...Rc8. Gukesh had just taken 6m 39s over the rook move 13.Ra1, giving Sindarov time to think as well. With a lead of over 16 minutes on the clock, going from 1h 38m to 1h 34m, Sindarov could afford a moderate think.

likely_reasons.reason: Several close options existed, and the top alternatives were pawn moves committing the structure while Be8 did not, so choosing between them may have taken some thought.
The game had left theory only two moves earlier with Sindarov's own 11...Qd8, so Sindarov was probably still calculating fresh positions, as the earlier long think on 12...Rc8 suggests.
A comfortable clock lead meant Sindarov could spend a few minutes without time pressure.

narrative.headline: Gukesh spends half an hour on 16.f3
narrative.text: Gukesh answered Sindarov's quick 15...f5, played in just 15 seconds, with the pawn move 16.f3 after a 29-minute, 29-second think, Gukesh's longest of the game. The engine rates it a good move: the evaluation dipped only slightly, from +0.11 to +0.01, with the game still level. The engine preferred the rook move Rfc1, but Gukesh had at least 5 good moves to choose from, including the pawn moves a5 and h3. Like f3, those pawn moves permanently change the pawn structure, which may be one likely reason Gukesh weighed things so carefully. The game was only four moves out of known theory after Sindarov left the book with 11...Qd8, so Gukesh was probably working things out over the board, as Gukesh did earlier when spending nearly 14 minutes on 12.O-O. The cost was steep: Gukesh's clock fell from 1h 19m to 49m 44s, while Sindarov still had 1h 26m.

likely_reasons.reason: Gukesh had at least five good options of different kinds, including several pawn moves that commit the pawn structure, so there was no single obvious choice.
The game had left opening theory only four moves earlier with Sindarov's 11...Qd8, so Gukesh probably had to rely on fresh calculation rather than preparation.
Sindarov's quick 15...f5 also changed the pawn structure, which may have prompted Gukesh to reassess the position before replying.

narrative.headline: Gukesh finds the engine's top move quickly
narrative.text: Gukesh played 20.Bg3 in just 19 seconds, and it was the engine's first choice, keeping the evaluation level at +0.08. The engine saw only two good moves here, 20.Bg3 and 20.Bf4, both bishop retreats, while the pawn push 20.f4 would have committed the pawn structure and dropped to -0.42. Because the two sensible options were similar quiet retreats, the choice probably did not need deep calculation. Sindarov had just played the quiet knight retreat 19...Nd7 in 16 seconds, which may not have changed the position much. Gukesh had already spent big chunks of time earlier, including 29m 29s on 16.f3 and 13m 57s on 12.O-O, and was about 39 minutes behind on the clock, so moving briskly likely made practical sense.

likely_reasons.reason: The two good options were both non-committal bishop retreats, so the decision was fairly simple.
Sindarov's previous move was a quiet knight retreat that probably did not demand fresh calculation.
Gukesh was well behind on the clock after earlier long thinks, which likely encouraged a quick move.
